title: Application of Formal Methods (SAT/SMT) to the Design of Constrained Codes
problem: Constrained coding design requires hardware-efficient translation logic between restricted and unrestricted code spaces while minimizing transmission error effects.
motivation: High-speed communication links need efficient constrained codes balancing bit efficiency and transmission rates through optimized hardware translation.
method: Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) formulation automates translation logic design by minimizing complexity and error impact while achieving hardware efficiency, reducing design time from weeks to hours.
key_novelty: SMT-based automation of constrained code hardware design eliminates manual error-prone IR translation.
contributions: SMT formulation for constrained coding translation logic design
Error resilience in decoded output optimization
Development time reduction from weeks to hours

metrics.other: development time reduced weeks to hours

limitations: Initial results only; detailed performance comparisons not discussed.
primary_theme: formal methods for communication codec design automation
